grades.quote: This includes read-only 0 behavior for any bits undefined by any implemented standard extensions.
grades.reason: Only tangentially related. It describes hardware behavior for custom CTR extension bits: undefined bits read as 0 when the custom bits are zero. It gives no guidance on what software should do with reserved or unsupported fields.

grades.quote: Each `xenvcfg` register is WARL; however, software should determine the legal values from the execution environment discovery mechanism.
grades.reason: Tells software how to handle fields whose legal values are implementation-dependent. The xenvcfg fields are WARL, so software should find the legal values through the execution environment discovery mechanism. This is useful but narrow, because it covers one register family and does not cover reserved fields.
Exploration project exercises from an OS textbook introduction. It has nothing to do with control-register fields.

grades.quote: the range of supported values can be determined by attempting to write a desired setting then reading to see if the value was retained.
grades.reason: Directly addresses unsupported values in control register fields. WARL fields accept any written value and always read back a legal one. Software can find the supported values by writing a setting and reading it back. Writing an unsupported value raises no exception. It does not cover WPRI reserved fields, but it answers the unsupported-field half of the question.
